name: Silent Threads Security
author: silenthreads

sections.description:
Silent Threads Security watches your site for malware, blocks attacks before they reach WordPress, and helps you close the gaps attackers look for.

Free features

  • Malware scanner (quick and standard scans) with signatures updated from the Silent Threads cloud
  • Automatic scheduled scans (every 7 hours by default, or daily, every 3 days or weekly) with email summaries, and full scan history
  • Web application firewall with SQL injection, XSS and other attack rules
  • Core file integrity check against the official WordPress.org checksums, with one-click repair
  • Vulnerability scanner for plugins, themes and WordPress core, with alerts for newly published vulnerabilities
  • Database, configuration, attack surface and persistence (backdoor) scanners
  • Login protection: brute-force lockout, two-factor authentication, strong password policy
  • Hardening checklist, activity log, file change monitoring and backups
  • Email alerts and a security dashboard

Free license

The plugin downloads malware signatures and firewall rules from the Silent Threads cloud service, so each site needs a free license key. After activation, enter your email address on the welcome screen and the key is emailed to you. The free license is free forever and there is no limit on the number of sites. Details of what is sent are listed under “External services” below.

Paid plans

Paid plans (Basic, Pro and Agency) come with the Silent Threads Security Pro add-on, available from silenthreads.com. Basic adds deep and full scans, a custom alert schedule, a custom login URL, login reCAPTCHA and real-time signature and firewall-rule updates. Pro adds secret and card-skimmer scanners, session protection and more. Agency adds a multi-site hub. This plugin works fully on its own without it.

External services

This plugin connects to the following external services. Nothing is sent to a service until the related feature is used, as described below.

Silent Threads licensing and threat-feed service (silenthreads.com)

Used to issue and verify your license, and to download malware signatures and firewall (WAF) rules.
* When you register for a license: your email address and site URL are sent.
* When the license is verified (on activation and about every 12 hours afterwards) and when signatures and firewall rules are downloaded: your license key, site URL, plugin version, WordPress version and PHP version are sent.
* Country lookups (OFF by default, opt-in): only if you turn on “country lookups” under Settings, the IP addresses shown in the firewall, login and activity-log screens are sent to look up their country. Nothing is sent unless you enable this. Results are cached for 30 days.
* Optional attack sharing (off by default, can be turned on in the firewall settings): IP addresses of blocked attackers, hit counts and the IDs of the rules they triggered are sent to improve the shared blocklist.
Terms of Service: https://silenthreads.com/terms
Privacy Policy: https://silenthreads.com/privacy

WPVulnerability (wpvulnerability.net)

Used to check installed plugins, themes and WordPress core for known vulnerabilities. The names and versions of installed components are sent when a vulnerability check runs.
Service and terms: https://www.wpvulnerability.net/

WordPress.org (api.wordpress.org, downloads.wordpress.org, wordpress.org)

Used to fetch official checksums for core and plugin integrity checks, and to download original core files when you click “Repair”. Your WordPress version and the slugs and versions of the plugins being checked are sent.
Privacy Policy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/

Have I Been Pwned – Pwned Passwords (api.pwnedpasswords.com)

Used by the strong password policy to check whether a password appears in known data breaches. Only the first 5 characters of the password’s SHA-1 hash are sent; the password itself never leaves your site.
Terms: https://haveibeenpwned.com/API/v3#AcceptableUse
Privacy Policy: https://haveibeenpwned.com/Privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins > Add New, or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it from the Plugins screen.
  3. Follow the welcome screen to get your free license key by email, or enter a key you already have.
  4. Run your first scan from Silent Threads Security > Dashboard.
sections.faq:
Is the plugin really free?

Yes. All features listed under “Free features” work with the free license. The license only connects your site to the signature and firewall-rule updates.

Why do I need a license key for the free version?

Signatures and firewall rules are served from our cloud. The key lets us deliver updates to real sites and keep the service fast and free of abuse.

Will it slow my site down?

Scans run in the background in small batches. The firewall runs before WordPress loads and adds very little time to each request.

I bought Pro. What do I do?

Download the Pro add-on from your account at silenthreads.com, upload it under Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin and activate it. Keep this plugin active as well; the add-on builds on it.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New console design for every admin screen: status bar, tab rails, KPI strip, tables, forms, notices, the activation pop-up and the setup wizard. Settings, data and behaviour are unchanged.
  • Pro-only settings are shown as locked cards (with the plan that includes them) when the site’s plan does not include them.
  • Clearer activation wording: scanning and the firewall run without activation; activating connects cloud protection (signature and firewall rule updates).
  • Secret values in Pro screens are masked, with a Show button.
  • Much faster admin pages on hosts where PHP has no sodium extension: the activation signature is now checked once per page load instead of on every check (a typical page went from about 27 seconds to under 2).
  • New email design for every alert, report and code email: Silent Threads logo, the brand colours, and a layout that fits phones. Plain-text copies are still included. Alert emails now show the severity, site, time and a button to open the dashboard.
  • The WAF attack report now shows each IP’s real attack count (it showed 0).
  • The Silent Threads logo is now the menu icon in the WordPress admin sidebar.
  • Fixed: in the setup wizard, Apply Selected (Hardening), Send Test Alert (Alerts) and the first-scan step did nothing, because their scripts were never printed on the wizard page. The hardening step now also lists what was applied and what failed.
  • Safer hardening on every web server: access rules now work on both Apache 2.4 and 2.2 (the old wp-config rule returned HTTP 500 on Apache 2.4 servers without mod_access_compat). If a server rejects a new .htaccess rule (HTTP 500), the rule is removed again automatically and reported. On Nginx, the wizard explains which four items need a server rule instead of ticking them.
  • Attack map: explains why countries are missing (country lookups off, plugin not activated, or the location service unreachable) with a link to fix it, instead of showing “Locating attackers” forever. Failed logins are no longer counted twice.
  • Notification bell: long file paths wrap, and the panel has a fixed height (480px, less on short screens) with its own vertical scrollbar.
  • Fixed: saving “country lookups” (and regenerating the API key) went to a page that does not exist (“Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page”). It now returns to the same screen with a “Saved” message. The setting itself was always saved.
  • Report emails on phones: tables keep their desktop layout and scroll sideways instead of squeezing every column into a few letters per line.
  • Email delivery: new “Email delivery” card in Settings with a test email and what this server uses to send (PHP mail() or an SMTP plugin; no SMTP plugin is required). Failed emails are logged with the recipient masked and explained in plain words (for example “Could not instantiate mail function”, which means PHP’s mail() failed on the server), and an admin notice warns that outgoing mail may not be working until an email goes through again or it is dismissed. An error inside the mail system can no longer stop a scan, firewall task or scheduled job. Success messages now say the email was accepted by the mail system, not that it was delivered.
  • Notification settings and the wizard’s Alert Setup: toggles, labels and fields line up, wizard fields use the full width, and checkboxes match the theme.
  • Hardening Center score and other gauges are readable on the dark theme; remaining blue accents, focus rings and button glows now use the Silent Threads colours.

1.0.0

  • First release on WordPress.org.
  • Malware scanner, web application firewall, core file integrity check, vulnerability scanner, login protection, two-factor authentication, hardening, backups and activity log.
  • Automatic scheduled scans, vulnerability alerts and full scan history.
